persona.name: Nico
persona.tagline: Late twenties, young professional, the car is an expression of who he is
persona.intro: My car says something about me. I don't want to blend in with every other small EV in the car park. It has to look sharp, feel a bit special inside, and have some edge when I drive.
persona.background: Nico is in his late twenties and early in a career he is proud of. The car is part of how he presents himself: he wants to stand out and to feel character when he drives. He has looked at the MINI because friends have one. He would never say out loud that he wants to be noticed, but it shows in every choice he makes. Never sell him on retro charm, that is the MINI's ground; he responds to contemporary edge.

motives.revealLine: Honestly, I want something that's clearly mine. When I pull up, people should know it's me.
I notice design. A car has to look sharp and intentional, not bland.
I want to feel something when I drive, a bit of edge, not just A to B.

nudgeLines: Hm, yes or no doesn't really get you far with me. Ask me something I can talk about.
That's a bit of a checkbox question. What do you actually want to know about me?
I could answer that with one word. Try asking me why, or how.

categories.title: First impression
prompts: Stand ten metres away from both cars. Which one draws the eye first, and why?
Find the copper details on the CUPRA. What do they signal compared to the MINI's chrome and round shapes?
Look at the wheels and stance. Which car looks like it wants to move?

categories.title: Inside
prompts: Sit in both driver seats. Which one holds you, which one just carries you?
Compare materials at eye level and where your hands rest.
Switch on the ambient lighting. What mood does each interior set?

categories.title: Character
prompts: Which car would Nico's colleagues recognise as 'his'?
Find one detail on each car that a designer would notice and appreciate.
Spot the visible VZ cues on the CUPRA: badges, wheels, seats, steering wheel. What do they promise before you even drive?

persona.name: Sara
persona.tagline: Early thirties, the car is her personal space, quality she can touch and a moment for herself
persona.intro: My drive home is my moment to switch off. I want the car to feel calm and well made, a place I enjoy being in, not just something that gets me there.
persona.background: Sara is in her early thirties. The car is her personal space, above all on the drive home after work. She values quality she can touch and a small sense of occasion in everyday life. She is comparing the smart because it is the sensible urban choice everyone recommends. Never sell her on small and practical, that is the smart's ground; she responds to sensuality, quality feel and an elevated everyday experience.

topics: how she feels in the car
motives.revealLine: My drive home is my moment. I want the car to feel calm and good to be in.
I notice how things feel. Cheap plastics bother me, I want it to feel well made.
I'd like something that feels a bit special every day, not just functional.

nudgeLines: I could just say yes to that. Ask me in a way that lets me tell you a bit more.
That feels like a form I'm filling in. What are you curious about?
Short answer: it depends. Ask me why, and I'll tell you.

categories.title: Quality you can touch
prompts: Close the doors of both cars. Listen and feel the difference.
Run your hand along the dashboard, the door cards and the centre console in both cars.
Compare the seat materials and stitching.

categories.title: Sound and mood
prompts: Play the same track on both sound systems. Which one would Sara want for her drive home?
Switch on the ambient lighting in the evening setting.
Which cabin feels like a place to spend time in?

categories.title: Character
prompts: Which car looks 'cute' and which looks 'grown-up with an edge'?
Find the CUPRA details that a smart owner would not expect.
Sit in the CUPRA driver seat, hands on the wheel. Does the driving position promise something the smart doesn't?
